problem: Suppose that $L$ is a linear differential operator such that $L({y}_{1})={x}^{2}-3x$ and $L({y}_{2})=x(x+1)$ for some functions ${y}_{1}(x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x).$ What is $L({y}_{1}+3{y}_{2})?$
worked_solution:
For any linear differential operator,

$$
L(a{y}_{1}(x)+b{y}_{2}(x))=aL({y}_{1}(x))+bL({y}_{2}(x))
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants. 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L({y}_{1}+3{y}_{2}) & =L({y}_{1})+3L({y}_{2}) \\  & ={x}^{2}-3x+3\cdot x(x+1) \\  & ={x}^{2}-3x+3{x}^{2}+3x \\  & =({x}^{2}+3{x}^{2})+(3x-3x) \\  & =4{x}^{2}+0 \\  & =4{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
